conventions.frame: ENU metres about the bbox centre, x east, y north, z up
conventions.ring: exterior rings are CCW and not closed; the outward normal of an edge with unit tangent t is n = (t_y, -t_x)
conventions.axes: rows of the Rodrigues matrix of computed_rotation are the camera right, down and forward directions in ENU; the matrix is world to camera
conventions.projection_spherical: d = P - C, c = axes * d, u = 0.5 + atan2(c_x, c_z) / 2pi, v = 0.5 + asin(c_y / |d|) / pi
conventions.wall_key: <building key>_<edge index>, plus p<k> when the wall was split

files.what: the run frame: bbox centre lon0/lat0 and the sphere radius. x = (lon - lon0) * pi/180 * R * cos(lat0), y = (lat - lat0) * pi/180 * R
Params from common.py with the values of the reference run; the Rust Params::default() must match this field for field
the raw Overpass answer the run consumed; input to geometry, not a product
the Graph API image records the run consumed, trimmed to the fields the geometry and pose stages read, in the shape the API answers with; input, not a product. Sorted by id

one record per footprint in the run frame: exterior ring CCW and not closed, holes, ring node ids in ring order, OSM height and its source, min_height, and whether the footprint touches the unpadded bbox

every wall of the box: endpoints a and b in ENU metres, outward normal, length, the OSM node ids of the merged span, the original ring edges with their s intervals, the OSM height, and the split piece index

the end of the pipeline per wall: tier, confidence, the panos fused, the grid size, the unknown share and the reason codes. Not an input to any stage; it says which walls the later golden tests must get right

cameras straight out of pose.camera_from_meta, before sfm.py replaces the centre by the cluster shot centre. axes rows are the camera right, down and forward directions in ENU; C is computed_geometry with computed_altitude as z; cam_height_m is the class prior (2.5 m rig, 1.4 m phone). Sorted by id

the same cameras after sfm.py: C is the mapped cluster shot centre and ground_z / cam_height_m come from the cloud. The difference against cameras_pose.json is exactly what the sfm stage owes. The camera model is not repeated; join on id with cameras_pose.json. Sorted by id

every (wall, camera) pair the geometric stage looked at on the kept walls. gate_pass and gate_value are parallel to the file's own gate_names list, with null where a gate does not apply: outward, near, far, incidence and angwidth always; fov only on perspective and brown cameras; nadir and zenith always, carrying the rig band for a panorama and repeating the fov fraction for a phone. The image gates (blur, exposure, vegetation) run later and are not here. Kept walls are the textured ones, the ones with a candidate that passed every gate, and every fourth of the rest, which on this box keeps all 111 walls that have any candidate. Sorted by wall then pano

the align stage. candidates.json holds every candidate of every wall with the value and verdict of every gate from the registered centres, its visible span, and the view list the run selected in order; cameras.json the registered camera each candidate names; reg.json plus points/ the whole facade band of a sample of panos, which is what register_pano searches, with every number the acceptance test produced, `sampled` saying what a 4000-point subsample of the same band would have decided instead, and the cluster-wide fallback band and shift for the clusters that sample reaches. Points are little endian float32 xy pairs in the run frame

the preview crop and the image gates of a spread of (wall, candidate) pairs, with everything they were rendered from: the source thumbnail, the registered camera, the wall moved onto that candidate's own plane fit, the per view foot z, the visible span and the depth map (16-bit PNG of the float16 bit pattern). The products are every gate value and the pixel count of every occlusion bit; the first few also carry the RGB crop, the occlusion byte plane and the vegetation mask

the distinct non-spherical camera models in the box with the largest normalised radius |(x/z, y/z)| each one maps injectively (pose.radial_limit: 0.9 times the first root of 1 + 3 k1 r^2 + 5 k2 r^4 + 7 k3 r^6, capped at 6.0)

one real camera of each model with sample world points and the pixel each one lands on. u and v are normalised (px = u * width, py = v * height); a null u means no projection at all, which is a point behind the camera or past the radial limit. The spherical case also carries the inverse map from pixel to unit world direction

sample finished walls: <key>.png is 1 px per metre with the facade colour in RGB and the class in alpha (255 wall, 192 window, 128 door, 64 unknown, 0 no data), <key>_cls.png the class channel alone, <key>_tex.png the 8 px per metre texture, <key>.json the per wall record
